statement_record.book: Definition 5.31: a functor F : C → D creates limits of type J if for every diagram C : J → C and every limiting cone (p_j : L → F C_j) in D there is a UNIQUE cone (p̄_j : L̄ → C_j) in C with F(L̄) = L and F(p̄_j) = p_j, and that unique cone is itself a limit for the diagram in C. Creating colimits is the dual/analogous notion.
statement_record.intree: No general definition exists. The notion appears only in instantiated form: [CreatesUSplitCoequalizers] (Beck.v:164) is creation specialized to coequalizers of U-split pairs, with the on-the-nose clause deliberately replaced by an iso-compatible one ('every iso-compatible lift be colimiting', header line 52-58); [equivalence_creates_limits] (Equivalence/Limit.v:486) is the map Limit (F ◯ G) → Limit G for an equivalence F, i.e. the existence half only, for one specific class of functors; [CreatedSplitCoequalizer] (BeckObjects.v:385) is the concrete created-data record at EM_Forget; and Construction/Comma/Limit.v proves the comma projection creates J-limits but exposes only the packaged conclusion [Comma_Complete].
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: (i) there is no functor-and-shape-indexed definition 'F creates J-limits' — nothing in Structure/Limit/Preservation.v beyond [PreservesLimit], [PreservesColimit], [PreservesAllLimits/Colimits] and [ReflectsIsos]; (ii) where creation IS defined ([CreatesUSplitCoequalizers]) it is fixed to one diagram shape (a U-split parallel pair) and the book's on-the-nose equalities F(L̄)=L, F(p̄)=p are relaxed to 'up to a compatible isomorphism i : U q ≅ scoeq_obj S', an explicit and documented weakening forced by setoid morphism equality; (iii) [equivalence_creates_limits] delivers only the existence half (a limit of G upstairs) and asserts nothing about uniqueness of the lifted cone, and applies only to equivalences; (iv) the colimit dual is present only through these same two special cases.

gap: The general definition of Definition 5.31 — a predicate/class 'F creates limits of type J' quantified over an arbitrary shape J and an arbitrary functor F, with the uniqueness clause on the lifted cone and the requirement that the lift be limiting, plus its colimit dual — is not in the library. What exists is (a) the shape-fixed class [CreatesUSplitCoequalizers], whose uniqueness clause is weakened from on-the-nose to iso-compatible, (b) [equivalence_creates_limits]/[equivalence_creates_colimits], existence-only and restricted to equivalences, and (c) an unpackaged creation argument inside Construction/Comma/Limit.v whose exported conclusion is only completeness of the comma category. Consequently nothing in-tree can state 'U creates limits' as a hypothesis or a conclusion in the generality Awodey's Proposition 5.32 and the monadicity literature require.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition CMon_Biproduct (M N : CMonObject) : @Biproduct CMon CMon_Zero M N := @Build_Biproduct CMon CMon_Zero M N (CMon_product M N) (CMon_inl M N) (CMon_inr M N) (CMon_exl M N) (CMon_exr M N) ... (CMon_bi_is_product M N) (CMon_bi_is_coproduct M N).

(* The direct product M ⊕ N: the product setoid with componentwise unit and operation. *) Definition CMon_product (M N : CMonObject) : CMonObject. ... cmon_setoid := {| carrier := (carrier M * carrier N)%type ; is_setoid := @prod_setoid ... |}

[CMon_Biproducts]: the direct product M ⊕ N (product setoid, componentwise operation) is simultaneously a product — with the projections [fst], [snd] and the pairing a ↦ (f a, g a) — and a coproduct — with the injections a ↦ (a, 0) and b ↦ (0, b) and the copairing (a, b) ↦ f a + g b.

Record Biproduct (x y : C) := { biproduct_obj : C; ... bi_is_product : ∀ (z : C) (f : z ~> x) (g : z ~> y), ∃! h : z ~> biproduct_obj, (bi_exl ∘ h ≈ f) ∧ (bi_exr ∘ h ≈ g); bi_is_coproduct : ∀ (z : C) (f : x ~> z) (g : y ~> z), ∃! h : biproduct_obj ~> z, (h ∘ bi_inl ≈ f) ∧ (h ∘ bi_inr ≈ g) }.

(* The canonical comparison morphism from the coproduct to the product ... *) Definition can_comparison (x y : C) : x + y ~{C}~> x × y := ... (with Context (E : ∀ x y : C, IsIsomorphism (can_comparison x y)) as the semiadditivity hypothesis, line 324)
Program Definition CMon_Forget : CMon ⟶ Sets := {| fobj := fun M => cmon_setoid M; fmap := fun _ _ f => cmon_map f |}.

statement_record.book: Unnumbered remark following Proposition 5.32: the forgetful functor of an algebraic category does NOT create all colimits — witness the coproduct of abelian groups, whose underlying set is the PRODUCT of the underlying sets (G + H ≅ G × H), not their disjoint sum.
statement_record.intree: [CMon_Biproduct] exhibits, for commutative monoids, exactly the phenomenon: the direct product on the product setoid carries both [bi_is_product] and [bi_is_coproduct], so the binary coproduct in CMon is (carried by) the product of the underlying setoids. [can_comparison : x + y ~> x × y] with the semiadditivity hypothesis that it is invertible names the same coincidence abstractly, and [CMon_Forget : CMon ⟶ Sets] is the underlying-set functor.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in three ways: (i) the witness category is CMon (commutative monoids), not Ab — the library has no category of abelian groups (no negation layer above CMon, only [Structure/Additive.v] as an abstract class); (ii) the punchline is never drawn: nowhere is it said that [CMon_Forget] fails to preserve or create the binary coproduct, and indeed no preservation/creation statement about [CMon_Forget] exists at all (it is proved only faithful); (iii) the comparison with the coproduct of the underlying SETS (the disjoint union [Sets_Cocartesian]) is not made — no in-tree statement compares CMon_Forget (M + N) with CMon_Forget M + CMon_Forget N. The positive half of the remark (coproduct = product for the commutative algebraic structure) is present in full and constructively.

statement_record.book: Proposition 5.35: if D is an ω-CPO with a least element 0 and h : D → D is continuous, then h has a fixed point h(x) = x, and it is the least among all fixed points. Proof: take the chain d_0 = 0, d_{n+1} = h(d_n) (ascending because h is monotone and 0 ≤ d_0); continuity gives h(d_ω) = colim_n h(d_n) = colim_n d_{n+1} = d_ω; and for any fixed point x, 0 ≤ x and inductively d_{n+1} = h(d_n) ≤ h(x) = x, so d_ω ≤ x.
statement_record.intree: The same argument at full categorical generality: [Chain F : Omega ⟶ C] is the chain 0 → F0 → F²0 → … (Construction/Chain.v:33-64), and given a colimit [HL : IsAColimit (Chain F) A] together with [AdamekData] (the honest form of 'F preserves this colimit', pinning the shifted cocone's legs to the image legs), [adamek : @Initial (FAlg F)] makes (A, α) the INITIAL F-algebra; [lambek] then gives [F A ≅ A], the fixed-point conclusion, and initiality of the algebra is the leastness clause (in a poset, an F-algebra is a prefixed point F x ≤ x and a unique map into it is exactly A ≤ x).

evidence.intree_statement: Lemma monic_pullback_stable {C : Category} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (m : y ~> z) (Hm : Monic m) (P : Pullback f m) : Monic (pullback_fst f m P).
(* Monomorphisms are stable under pullback: in the square P --snd--> y, fst | | m, x --f--> z with m monic, the projection opposite m is monic as well. *)

Record Pullback {C : Category} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (g : y ~> z) := { Pull : C; pullback_fst : Pull ~> x; pullback_snd : Pull ~> y; pullback_commutes : f ∘ pullback_fst ≈ g ∘ pullback_snd; ump_pullbacks : ∀ Q (q1 : Q ~> x) (q2 : Q ~> y), f ∘ q1 ≈ g ∘ q2 → ∃! u : Q ~> Pull, pullback_fst ∘ u ≈ q1 ∧ pullback_snd ∘ u ≈ q2 }.
sub_is_monic := monic_pullback_stable f (sub_mono u) (sub_is_monic u) (pullback f (sub_mono u))  (* the inverse image of a subobject is a subobject *)

evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Part : Category := {| obj := Sets; hom := fun x y => @SetoidMorphism x (is_setoid x) (option y) (@option_setoid _ (is_setoid y)); homset := fun x y => @SetoidMorphism_Setoid x {| is_setoid := @option_setoid _ (is_setoid y) |} |}. This is the category PAR (also written Par or Pfn) of setoids and partial maps. Following the standard presentation, a partial map A ⇀ B is encoded as a total setoid map A → option B (= A → 1 + B): the elements sent to [None] are exactly those outside the domain of definition. Equivalently this is the Kleisli category of the maybe monad [option] on [Sets].

Program Definition Par : Category := {| obj := Type; hom := fun A B => A ~> option B; homset := fun P Q => {| equiv := fun f g => ∀ x, f x = g x |}; id := λ _, Some; compose := fun x y z f g => option_bind f ∘ g |}.

#[export] Program Instance Part_Cartesian : @Cartesian Part := { product_obj := fun x y => {| carrier := x + (y + (x * y)) |} }.  (with the header note that the categorical product in PAR is the 'classical product' A + B + (A × B), not the set product)

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the exercise's construction is PARAMETRIC in an arbitrary category C with pullbacks and is built from subobjects (equivalence classes of monos) with composition BY PULLBACK; the in-tree categories are two fixed concrete instances (setoids, Coq types) built from the maybe monad, where the 'domain of definition' is recovered only as the preimage of [Some] and no pullback and no subobject ever appears. The library's own header acknowledges the identification holds because Set is a Boolean topos ('in Set (a Boolean topos) every Kleisli map of [option] is a partial function, so PAR ≅ Kleisli(option)') — i.e. it is a coincidence of the concrete model, not the general construction. The generality the exercise asks to verify (any C with pullbacks) is therefore absent, as is the equivalence relation on (|f|, U_f) pairs.

evidence.intree_statement: (** Pushout of the span [y <-f- x -g-> z]. *) Definition IsPushout {x y z : C} (f : x ~> y) (g : x ~> z) : Type := @Pullback (C^op) y z x f g.

Lemma pushout_ump {x y z : C} {f : x ~> y} {g : x ~> z} (P : IsPushout f g) (Q : C) (q1 : y ~> Q) (q2 : z ~> Q) (Hcomm : q1 ∘ f ≈ q2 ∘ g) : ∃! u : pushout_apex P ~> Q, u ∘ pushout_in1 P ≈ q1 ∧ u ∘ pushout_in2 P ≈ q2. Proof. exact (@ump_pullbacks (C^op) y z x f g P Q q1 q2 Hcomm). Qed.

Class HasPushouts (C : Category) : Type := { pushout : forall {x y z : C} (f : x ~> y) (g : x ~> z), IsPushout f g }.  (with [HasPullbacks_op_of_HasPushouts] and [HasPushouts_of_HasPullbacks_op] exposing both directions of the definitional equivalence)
